messages.subject: GSOC 2011
messages.body_plain:
Dear R community,

I hope that this email list still is active - I wanted to start a discussion about GSOC 2011, and I think that you an appropriate target audience ...
I participated as a student last year and really learned a lot from this project; this year I could imagine mentoring a project.

As far as I can see, following next steps would have to be done for GSOC 2011 (according to last year's procedure):

- set up a GSOC 2011 page on R-Wiki
- find an organizer who manages R's application as a mentoring organization
- promote student applications in the R community

The timeline for the next steps is as following:

February 28: Mentoring organizations can begin submitting applications to Google.

March 11: Mentoring organization application deadline.

March 14-17: Google program administrators review organization applications.

March 18: List of accepted mentoring organizations published on the Google Summer of Code 2011 site.

March 28: Student application period opens.

April 8: Student application deadline.

Cheers,
Felix

messages.body_plain:
Hi Felix & Dear List,

> I hope that this email list still is active - I wanted to start a discussion
> about GSOC 2011, and I think that you an appropriate target audience ...
> I participated as a student last year and really learned a lot from this
> project; this year I could imagine mentoring a project.

Thanks.

Do you have a project in mind that you would like to mentor?

> As far as I can see, following next steps would have to be done for GSOC 2011
> (according to last year's procedure):
>
> - set up a GSOC 2011 page on R-Wiki

Could you do that, please?

> - find an organizer who manages R's application as a mentoring organization

Dirk is already active off-list: He convinced me that I want to be your admin
(on the conditions, though, that (a) there's a second admin and (b) I don't keep
anyone away who'd like to be admin).

> - promote student applications in the R community

r-devel knows that GSoC is announced.

Before telling r-help (and r-devel) that we are looking for students, we should
have a bunch of project proposals in the Wiki, I think.

However, students on this list may already
- propose projects and try to find a mentor
- signal interest in the projects that are announced by mentors-in-spe

I started to spread the rumour "looking for students" for two projects I have in
mind:

- my hyperSpec project still has lots of opportunities, also for quite different
tastes (GUI, spectroscopy-related, HPC, ...)

- I started to email with Hadley about a joint project between hyperSpec and
ggplot2: getting ggplot2 working with "foreign" data where long data.frames are
too inefficient, the spectra being one example.

Best regards

Claudia

messages.subject: Re: GSOC 2011
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

> Do you have a project in mind that you would like to mentor?

I want to propose an extension of my last year's project "Social Relations Analyses in R". This package already is used by many researchers, and we got several requests to extend the package to a new type of analyses (specifically - whoever's interested: SRA with roles - an approach which utilizes structural equation models to model specific types of SRAs).

> > As far as I can see, following next steps would have to be done for GSOC 2011
> > (according to last year's procedure):
> >
> > - set up a GSOC 2011 page on R-Wiki
> Could you do that, please?

Done - I basically copied last years page. I created a stub at http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2011 - I will add some more information about timeline, logo, etc., as well as my own proposal tomorrow.

> > - find an organizer who manages R's application as a mentoring organization
> Dirk is already active off-list: He convinced me that I want to be your admin (on the conditions, though, that (a) there's a second admin and (b) I don't keep anyone away who'd like to be admin).

Great! I could help you with that, as long as:
>  (b) I don't keep anyone away who'd like to be second admin.

Cheers,
Felix
